Subject: Proposal: committed wallet + ramp + grace window

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. FastPay is keen to move from pilot to a committed model but we need a drawdown structure that matches variable usage across our product launches. High level ask: a $1.2M committed wallet for 12 months (usage-based drawdown), with a clear ramp and a cure/grace window before penalties or throttles kick in.

Specifically we care about:
- Monthly drawdown cadence (we typically burst month-to-month during marketing pushes)
- Grace/cure period length before any rate changes or overage invoices
- Carryover or replenishment options if we under-spend early in the year
- Term discounts for 1yr vs 2yr vs 3yr commitments

I attached a simple token-velocity export and a starter schedule (Commit_Schedule_v1.xlsx). We can accept a staged ramp (frontloaded credits in Q1) if Redwood offers a modest term discount and a 30–60 day cure period.

Can you share a draft structure and an example of the SLA/penalty mechanics for a usage shortfall? We want predictable behavior (no sudden cutoffs) and prefer throttling down to a lower-priced tier rather than instant penalties.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Partnerships, FastPay

Elena —

Appreciate the details and the sheet. We’re definitely aligned on predictability and avoiding abrupt cutoffs. A couple quick clarifying questions so we can model pricing:

1) When you say "frontloaded credits in Q1" — do you mean credits applied to the wallet upfront (i.e., more of the $1.2M available early) or a billing credit schedule that reduces after Q1?
2) What is your expected month-to-month variance? The sample shows a 5x peak-to-trough across product launches — is that representative?
3) Do you want carryover of unused credits between years (if multi-year) or automatic replenishment on breach?

High-level we can propose: monthly drawdown from the wallet, a 45-day cure period (grace) before we move to a lower throughput SLA / lower-cost tier, and a true-up at the end of each 3-month window. But I want finance and pricing to weigh in — looping Lauren and Priya.

If possible, can you share a 12-month token forecast (even rough)? That’ll let us size the tier transitions and term discount math. I’ve cc'd Lauren for pricing and legal triggers.

I can put together a 2x/3x term discount table (1yr/2yr/3yr) and an ops playbook for velocity-based throttles. We can also include a one-time makewhole option for very large overages where adding extra capacity is required.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Answers inline:
1) Frontloaded credits: we prefer more of the wallet available upfront (apply credits at contract start). That helps when we launch new products.
2) Variance: yes, 3–6x is common; peaks align with campaigns but baseline is stable.
3) Carryover: prefer limited carryover (up to 15% annually) or an option to convert unused credits into a renewal discount.

Attached is a 12-month forecast (simple) — see tab "MonthlyForecast" in Commit_Schedule_v1.xlsx. We'd consider a 2-year commitment if Redwood can offer an additional ~7–10% term discount and clear operational rules for drawdown/penalty.

We prefer cure periods of 45–60 days rather than 30. Also, if usage drops significantly (greater than 70% from expected for 90 days) we are open to a negotiated throttling to a lower throughput SLA instead of a hard freeze.

Elena

Team —

Reviewed Elena’s ask and the forecast. Draft proposal and recommended ops mechanics below (copy into SOW draft once we agree):

Proposal summary (for FastPay, $1.2M wallet, 12mo base):
- Wallet drawdown: monthly decrement from prepaid wallet based on actual usage (token-equivalent).
- Ramp: frontload 30% of wallet at contract start, remaining released evenly over remaining months (option to reprofile if customer gives 60-day notice).
- Grace/cure: 45-day grace window after a breach trigger (90-day rolling usage < 60% of committed run-rate). During cure window we provide notice + throttled priority (no immediate penalty).
- Velocity corridor: If 90-day rolling usage < 40% of committed run-rate after cure, automatically shift to a lower-priced throughput tier (no retroactive charge), with ability to re-escalate to full tier on 30-day notice and payment of replenishment delta.
- Carryover: allow up to 15% carryover into next contract year (if multi-year), capped at $50k or equivalent tokens.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups; annual reconciliation for accounting.

Term discounts (suggested):
- 12-month: base price (no additional term discount beyond volume pricing)
- 24-month: additional 6% discount on base rates
- 36-month: additional 10% discount on base rates + 30-day price protection on major model upgrades

Operational notes for SOW/legal:
- Define breach as 90-day rolling average < 60% of committed run-rate for two consecutive windows.
- Cure begins on written notice; grace = 45 days from notice.
- Overage flow: if customer exceeds wallet before month-end, we bill overage at contracted OTC rate unless customer elects to top-up wallet.

Attachments: I’m publishing a refined schedule (Commit_Schedule_v2.xlsx) that includes a sample monthly drawdown example and tier thresholds. Also added a clean SOW_Draft.docx with placeholders for the velocity corridor language.

Next steps: Ben — please review pricing tiers with FastPay today. Karthik — can you run the margin impact for 24/36 months and confirm the max allowed carryover cap? Lauren — please note contract language we should avoid (no automatic refunds for under-spend; only credit conversion).

Priya
